newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to declare lawmaker a fugitive - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to declare lawmaker a fugitive - paper.

text.p: The Sri Lankan government plans to declare as fugitives an opposition politician and a former mayor over last week's assassination of a ruling coalition lawmaker, a senior minister was quoted on Sunday as saying.

Justice Minister G.L. Peiris told the state-owned Observer the government had enough evidence to file a legal complaint against the two suspects wanted for the killing of Nalanda Ellawala, 29, a member of parliament from the ruling Peoples Alliance (PA).
Peiris could not be immediately reached for comment.
Ellawala, the Indian Ocean island's youngest member of parliament, was cremated on Saturday at Ratnapura, a gem-mining town 80 km (50 miles) southeast of Colombo.
Police fired teargas and called in the army after some of the estimated 100,000 mourners set fire to shops, threw stones at the police station and damaged police vehicles.
Last Tuesday's killing of Ellawala during a roadside quarrel between his supporters and rivals of the main opposition United National Party (UNP) sparked two days of riots in Ratnapura.
Police said the area was calm on Sunday after they lifted an overnight curfew.

Police have offered a reward of one million rupees ($17,500) to anyone providing information leading to the arrest of the two suspects, UNP lawmaker Susantha Punchinilame and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, a former mayor of Ratnapura.
The two suspects were said to be planning to surrender through the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the independent Sunday Times reported.

Punchinilame, in a statement published in the paper, said he was prepared to surrender once his security was assured. He felt his life was in danger after mobs attacked his home and those of his supporters folliwng Ellawala's killing.
In the riots on Tuesday and Wednesday, police said pro-People's Alliance mobs had set fire to homes and buildings of UNP supporters. No one was hurt in the riots.

Ellawala was murdered the day before a deadline for filing nominations in the March 21 local elections, the first electoral contest between the UNP and the PA since 1994 when the alliance ended UNP's 17 years in power.
More than 18,000 candidates from 12 political parties, including the alliance, the UNP and 132 independent groups, plan to contest the polls for 238 local government assemblies.
The UNP suspended the party memberships of the two murder suspects the day after party leader and former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe called on the two to turn themselves in.
